strengths: Carefully designed 1D synthetic testbed enables rigorous mechanistic analysis of spatial reasoning in CLIP-style models while maintaining experimental control

Thorough attention decomposition analysis (Eq. 1-2) with clear visualization of horizontal gradients in positional-token cross-terms, backed by definitive ablations (Fig. 5e) showing necessity of these components
Surprising empirical finding that label diversity substantially outweighs layout diversity for generalization to unseen object pairs, challenging intuitive assumptions
Comprehensive evaluation across three well-defined generalization types with proper train-test separation, plus extensive ablations across architectural variants and positional encodings

Novel theoretical analysis extending findings to RoPE, identifying two distinct generalization mechanisms (bias-induced gradient and learned subspace alignment) with supporting evidence from PCA and singular value analysis
Excellent presentation quality with clear figures, comprehensive appendices, and transparent discussion of limitations
weaknesses: Extreme problem simplification (1D images, left-right relations only, artificial single-token text) creates substantial gap to realistic VLMs; unclear how findings transfer to 2D natural images and compositional language, with no concrete experimental pathway provided

Shallow models (1-4 Transformer blocks, 4 heads) studied; Appendix L acknowledges 2-layer analysis is incomplete, leaving uncertainty about mechanisms' scaling properties to realistic depths (e.g., ViT-B with 12 layers)

Modest unseen-pair generalization (~90-95% best case with high label diversity) and degraded performance with bilateral captions (Fig. 8) suggest mechanisms may be fragile or task-specific; unclear if robustness translates to natural settings

Text encoder analysis incomplete: Section 6 is brief, authors explicitly note 'complexity in interpreting 2-layer Transformer model' (p.8) remains unresolved, and alignment via learned rotation (Fig. 7) lacks principled explanation

RoPE mechanism verification is indirect (PCA/SVD analysis) rather than direct intervention; lacks empirical confirmation by explicitly manipulating model components (e.g., enforcing low-rank W_K) during training
Limited practical implications for improving real VLMs; no discussion of whether encouraging positional embeddings during training improves spatial reasoning, or guidance on architectural changes

Incomplete coverage of related work on positional encodings and spatial reasoning; no comparison with sinusoidal or other alternatives; connection to grokking phenomenon (Appendix B) mentioned but underdeveloped
Single-head vision transformer consistently fails (Appendix K); requirement for multi-head attention claimed but not mechanistically explained, limiting understanding of what properties are essential

strengths: Rigorous experimental design with a well-motivated 1D toy testbed that enables clean mechanistic analysis of spatial understanding
Thorough and novel mechanistic analysis identifying positional-token embedding interactions as critical for left-right symmetry breaking
Well-executed interpretability work including attention decomposition, ablations, and comparison of generalizing vs. non-generalizing models
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and honest discussion of limitations
Theoretical grounding (Appendix I) explaining why position-dependent gradients are necessary for OOD generalization, with extensions to modern positional encodings like RoPE
Strong finding that label diversity substantially outweighs layout diversity for generalization, suggesting interesting principles about semantic vs. positional variation
weaknesses: Severely limited scope—1D setting with only left-right relations and binary object pairs is far removed from realistic 2D spatial reasoning where the phenomenon actually matters
No empirical evidence that discovered mechanisms transfer to 2D images or more complex spatial relations, limiting practical applicability and generalizability
Key empirical finding (label >> layout diversity) lacks mechanistic explanation—why does semantic variety matter so much more than positional variety?
Architectural simplifications for mechanistic analysis (removing LayerNorm, MLP, using 1-layer models) reduce relevance to real models; 2-layer analysis acknowledged as incomplete
Theoretical analysis explains why position-dependent gradients are necessary but not why training discovers them—what loss signals drive this solution?
Limited practical implications for improving real VLMs on spatial reasoning tasks; paper contributes to understanding but not to system improvements
Important failure modes under-explored: why do 1-layer models fail with both left/right representations? Why is multi-head attention apparently necessary?
Some experimental gaps: the three generalization phases (Appendix C) are interesting but under-explored; connection to 'grokking' mentioned but not analyzed

strengths: Well-designed controlled 1D image-text testbed effectively isolates left-right spatial understanding mechanisms in a reproducible manner
Rigorous mechanistic analysis through attention logit decomposition (Eq. 1) systematically identifies contributions from token, positional, and bias components
Comprehensive ablation studies with multiple variants (weight decay, term removal, RoPE comparison, 2D/3D extensions) strengthen empirical findings
Clear mathematical framework for analyzing out-of-distribution generalization with explicit conditions (Eq. 14, 23) and validation (Figs. 19c-e)
Thorough documentation with 14 pages of appendices, clear hyperparameter specification, and reasonable reproducibility within controlled setting
Well-written paper with clear motivation, logical organization, and informative visualizations of attention patterns
weaknesses: Critical domain gap: 1D pixel-based synthetic setting is far removed from natural images; 2D extension (Appendix K) shows degraded performance with limited analysis, undermining claims about practical relevance

Oversimplified text representation using literal spatial descriptions (e.g., 'X is on the left of Y') rather than natural language; unclear how findings transfer to real VLM training with diverse linguistic descriptions

Limited evidence that discovered mechanisms generalize beyond synthetic data with learnable positional embeddings; RoPE-only variant (Fig. 18) shows substantially weaker results, suggesting findings are architecture-specific

Theoretical analysis of generalization mechanisms (especially Mechanism 2 on learned subspace alignment) relies on strong assumptions validated only indirectly through PCA analysis; causal claims lack definitive proof
Narrow scope limited to left-right relations in CLIP-style models; unclear whether mechanisms extend to other spatial relations, architectures, or VLM training paradigms
Unclear practical impact: no demonstration that mechanistic insights can improve spatial reasoning in real-world VLMs or downstream tasks; primarily of interest to interpretability specialists
No code release despite use of public codebases; integration details for 1D setting with standard frameworks incompletely specified
